successors.name: Tukulor Empire
successors.text: Ségou and its surroundings: the part of the empire left after Noukouma (the pages give no extent)

ledger.x: 1712: Mamari (Biton) Coulibaly founds the Bambara state at Ségou.
Undated, under Biton Coulibaly (1712-1755): he 'attacked Tomboctou, though he held the city only briefly.'
1751: the Mansa of Mali becomes a vassal.
Undated: Biton 'held the city only briefly', so Timbuktu is given up by Cliopatria's 1752 shape (page silent on the year).
1766: Ngolo Diarra seizes the throne from the Coulibaly line.
Between 1766 and 1790: Ngolo Diarra 'defeated the Macina Empire and re-established firm control over Djenne and Timbuktu.'
Between 1790 and 1808: Mansong Diarra 'earned renown as a great warrior, with defeats against several other groups, including Kaarta, Massina, Dogon, and Mossi.'
ledger.cp: Ardo of Massina and the Dogon

ledger.x: 1818: Seku Amadu's Fulani break Bambara power at Noukouma.
25 May 1860: Umar Tall's Tukulor army takes Nyamina.
The Mansa's vassalage ends at the latest with the empire.
10 March 1861: Ségou falls to Umar Tall.

wars.name: Biton Coulibaly's wars
wars.outcome: Conquests of the Fulani, Soninke, Mossi and of Macina, Beledougou, Djenné, Bamako (undated); a Kong invasion beaten in 1725; Timbuktu attacked and held only briefly; the Mansa of Mali made a vassal after Niani in 1751.

wars.name: Ségou succession wars
wars.outcome: 'Civil war and short reigns' under Dinkoro and Ali until Ngolo Diarra seized the throne in 1766; no land recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Ngolo Diarra's wars
wars.outcome: Ngolo 'defeated the Macina Empire and re-established firm control over Djenne and Timbuktu' (undated); he died in a campaign against the Mossi in 1790 (the Park passage implies 1795).

wars.name: Mansong Diarra's wars
wars.outcome: Defeats against Kaarta, Massina, the Dogon and the Mossi, all undated; the outline grows to 105k km2 in Cliopatria.

wars.name: Fulani jihad of Massina (Battle of Noukouma)
wars.outcome: Seku Amadu's Fulani rout the Bambara at Noukouma and take Djenné and the Mopti country; the Massina Empire is founded (Hamdullahi built 1820).

wars.name: Umar Tall's conquest of Ségou
wars.outcome: Nyamina falls on 25 May 1860, the Bambara army loses at Witala in September 1860, and Ségou falls on 10 March 1861.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Bamana frontier; the Ségou-Mopti heartland is known, the Niger bend, Dogon and Mossi edges are approximate.
